# Acceptable Use

## Company devices

A company laptop is for company work. Light personal use is tolerated where it does not affect work, breach another policy, or store personal data that the user would not want backed up. The backup service copies the profile folders, so personal tax files and personal photos kept there will be copied onto company storage.

## Data

Company data stays in company systems: the mailbox, the shared drives and the approved software. It is not copied to personal email, personal cloud storage or removable media. A genuine need to move data out, for example a regulator requesting a file, goes through the data-handling

## Accounts

Each person uses their own account. Sharing a password, letting a colleague work under your sign-in, or using a shared mailbox credential for ordinary mail breaches this policy. The password policy describes the approved store, SW-PWM-01.

Traffic on the VPN and on CORP-WIFI is logged. The logs are used for fault finding and for security investigations. They are not used for measuring working hours.

# Backup and Restore

## What is backed up

The backup service covers the home drive, the desktop and the documents folder of every company laptop, plus the shared drives. It runs every two hours while the device is online and on the VPN or on CORP-WIFI. A laptop that stays offline keeps a local cache of changes for seven days and uploads them at the next connection.

Mail is not part of this service. Mail retention is handled by the mailbox platform and is described in the email note.

# Email and Mailboxes

## Quotas

A user mailbox holds 50 GB. A shared mailbox holds 100 GB. At 90 percent full the owner gets a warning; at 100 percent the mailbox stops accepting mail. Archive mail older than one year to the online archive, which does not count against the quota.

## Shared mailboxes

A shared mailbox has its own credential, held by the mailbox owner. Members are granted access; they do not learn the password. Send-as is turned on only when the owner asks, and it is reviewed every six months.

## Forwarding and auto-replies

Forwarding to a personal address is blocked by rule. Forwarding to another company mailbox is allowed and must be visible to the sender, so silent redirects are rejected. Out-of-office replies should name the person covering and should not include a personal phone number.

## Retention

Mail is kept for seven years, including deleted items, because of the finance retention rule. A user cannot shorten this. A legal hold stops deletion entirely until the legal team releases it, and a hold is recorded against the mailbox rather than against one folder.

# Incident Severity

## The four levels

Severity describes impact, not how annoyed a caller is. The service desk sets it when the ticket is opened and can change it later.

SEV-1 is a complete loss of a core service for a large part of the company, or a confirmed exposure of sensitive data. Examples are the mail platform down for every site, or the VPN gateway rejecting all connections. SEV-1 pages the on-call lead immediately, at any hour.

SEV-2 is a core service degraded or unavailable for one site or one business unit, with a workaround that is painful. An example is one office

for one site or one business unit, with a workaround that is painful. An example is one office unable to reach shared drives while other offices work normally.

SEV-3 is a fault with a workaround that lets the user carry on, such as one laptop that will not take the VPN while a spare machine works. Most service-desk tickets are SEV-3.

SEV-4 is a request or a cosmetic fault: a software install, a quota increase, a label printed wrong. SEV-4 follows the request queue rather than the incident queue.

# Known Outages and Planned Maintenance

## How outages are announced

Planned work is posted to the status page and to the all-hands chat at least three working days ahead. Emergency work is posted as it starts, with the severity taken from the incident note. The status page is reachable without the VPN so that a VPN fault can still be read about.

## Standing windows

The directory and the VPN gateway are patched on the second Tuesday of each month, between 22:00 and 23:30 India time. During that window a reconnect may be needed and a certificate warning is expected; it is

India time. During that window a reconnect may be needed and a certificate warning is expected; it is not ERR-VPN-809. Mail is not patched in the same window.

Shared-drive firmware is updated on the first Sunday of each quarter, from 06:00 to 08:00 India time. Open files may be disconnected. Save and close large files before leaving on Friday.

## Current advisory

There is no standing advisory beyond the windows above. A fault that matches nothing posted on the status page is a new incident and should be ticketed with its error code rather than waited out.

# Leaver Offboarding

## On the last day

The manager confirms the leave in the HR system before the end of the last working day. At 18:00 local time the account is disabled, active VPN sessions are dropped, and the authenticator enrolment is revoked. Mail to the address bounces, unless the manager has nominated a shared mailbox to receive it for the next 30 days.

## Equipment

The laptop, dock and badge are returned on the last day at an office, or collected by courier within five working days for a remote leaver. The drive is wiped in the build room and the

within five working days for a remote leaver. The drive is wiped in the build room and the wipe certificate is filed against the asset. A device not returned within fifteen working days is escalated to the manager and then to payroll.

The leaver's files on shared drives stay where they are. Their home drive is archived for 90 days and then deleted, unless a legal hold applies. Membership of every group, including the VPN group, is removed the same evening. A contractor whose end date arrives is treated as a leaver even if no one confirms it.

# Password and MFA Policy (2026)

This policy replaces the 2025 version. Where the two differ, this document wins for any request dated 6 January 2026 or later.

## Password rules

A network password must be at least 14 characters long. It must contain lowercase letters, uppercase letters and a digit. Symbols are allowed but no longer required. # Printing and the Follow-me Queue

## The queue

Every office prints through one follow-me queue, named PRINT-FOLLOWME. The user sends the job from the laptop and releases it at any device on that floor by tapping their badge. Jobs that nobody releases are deleted after four hours and are not recoverable.

Colour printing is allowed. Jobs over fifty pages ask for confirmation on the device panel, to catch accidents.

## Secure documents

A job marked confidential is held in a separate lane and requires the badge plus the network PIN. It is deleted after one hour rather than four. Do not print credentials, and do not print customer

It is deleted after one hour rather than four. Do not print credentials, and do not print customer data that the ticket can link to instead.

## Faults

A jam, a streak, or an offline device is reported on the small-form code displayed on the printer itself. Quote the printer asset tag, which starts with the site code. Do not switch the printer off to clear a jam; open the panel shown on the screen.

## Home and VPN

There is no supported way to print to a home printer while the VPN is connected, because split tunnelling is off. Print before connecting, or print to PRINT-FOLLOWME

## Response and restore targets

The clock starts when the ticket is logged, not when the user first noticed the fault. Times below are working time for SEV-3 and SEV-4, and elapsed time for SEV-1 and SEV-2.

SLA-P1 covers SEV-1. First response is within 15 minutes and the restore target is 4 hours. A named incident lead publishes an update every 30 minutes until the service is back.

SLA-P2 covers SEV-2. First response is within 1 hour and the restore target is 8 hours.

SEV-2. First response is within 1 hour and the restore target is 8 hours. Updates go out every 2 hours.

SLA-P3 covers SEV-3. First response is within 4 working hours and the target resolution is 3 working days.

SLA-P4 covers SEV-4. First response is within 1 working day and the target fulfilment is 5 working days. A software request under review uses this target, and the ten-day security review sits inside it.

## When the clock pauses

The clock pauses when the desk is waiting on the user for a decision or for access to

pauses

The clock pauses when the desk is waiting on the user for a decision or for access to the machine, and it resumes when the user replies. It does not pause while the desk waits on an internal team.

## Missed targets

A missed SLA-P1 or SLA-P2 target is reviewed the next working day by the service owner. A missed SLA-P3 or SLA-P4 target is reported in the weekly queue review. Missing a target does not by itself change the severity.

Standard examples are the Cisco AnyConnect client SW-VPN-AC, the password manager SW-PWM-01, and the Office suite SW-OFFICE-365. Managed examples are the design suite SW-DESIGN-04 and the database IDE SW-DBIDE-02.

# Remote Access VPN

## Who may connect

Every employee and every approved contractor uses the corporate VPN before opening an internal system from outside an office. The only approved client is Cisco AnyConnect, listed in the catalogue as SW-VPN-AC. Split tunnelling is off, so all traffic from the laptop travels through the gateway while the session is up.

A session lasts twelve hours and then drops. Reconnect with the same method. Do not leave a session running on a shared or borrowed machine.

## How to connect

1. Open Cisco AnyConnect from the Start menu or the Applications folder.
2. The gateway address is

Open Cisco AnyConnect from the Start menu or the Applications folder.
2. The gateway address is vpn.corp.example.com. Type it once; the client remembers it.
3. Sign in with your corporate email address and your network password, then approve the push notification from the authenticator app.
4. Wait until the padlock icon turns green before you open Outlook, SAP or a file share.

If the push notification never arrives, wait thirty seconds and request it again. Three failed approvals lock the VPN sign-in for fifteen minutes.

Error codes

If the code remains, the machine certificate has expired and the service desk must re-enrol it. Quote ERR-VPN-809 when you raise the ticket.

ERR-VPN-412 means the account is not in the remote-access group. New starters are added on their first day by onboarding, and the group change can take one hour to reach the gateway. Quote ERR-VPN-412

the group change can take one hour to reach the gateway. Quote ERR-VPN-412 if it still fails after that hour.

ERR-VPN-102 means the gateway rejected the password. Reset the password through the self-service page rather than guessing again, because five wrong passwords lock the account.

## Split tunnelling and home use

Split tunnelling stays off because the data-loss controls only see traffic that passes the gateway. A user who needs a local printer at home should print before connecting, or use the follow-me print queue described in the printer note, which works over the tunnel.

Personal streaming and personal cloud backups are blocked by the gateway while the VPN is up. Disconnect when the work is finished.

## Contractors and travel

Contractors use the same client and the same gateway, but their access group expires on the contract end date. An expired group returns ERR-VPN-412 even when the password is correct. The sponsoring manager extends the date in the identity console.

Roaming abroad needs no extra setting. The gateway accepts connections from every country the company operates in. A connection from anywhere else is refused and the security team is notified.

# Office Wi-Fi

## Networks

Offices broadcast two networks. CORP-WIFI is for company laptops and uses certificate authentication, so there is no password to type or share. CORP-GUEST is for visitors and personal phones. A guest pass lasts eight hours, is created by any employee from the intranet, and throttles each device to 5 megabits per second.

## Connecting a company laptop

Company laptops are preconfigured for CORP-WIFI and connect on their own inside any office. If a laptop keeps associating and then dropping, forget the network and restart. Do not create a manual profile and

keeps associating and then dropping, forget the network and restart. Do not create a manual profile and do not type a password, because CORP-WIFI has none.

## What is blocked

CORP-WIFI blocks peer-to-peer file sharing and wireless displays that are not on the approved list. CORP-GUEST blocks access to every internal system, including the intranet and shared drives. A visitor who needs to show an internal document uses a company laptop, not the guest network.

## Coverage problems

Report a dead spot to the facilities portal with the floor and the nearest desk number. A single user whose colleagues connect fine is a

facilities portal with the floor and the nearest desk number. A single user whose colleagues connect fine is a device problem and goes to the service desk instead. Home Wi-Fi is the user's own; the company does not support it beyond the VPN note.
